question: In deep causal Post-Norm decoder Transformers, what drives token representations toward rank collapse at initialization, why do gradients fail to restore token diversity after collapse begins during training, and what loss and stationarity properties characterize the collapsed state?

key_findings.claim: Under a prefix-averaging and equal-correlation surrogate, causal attention strictly increases token similarity at initialization, while the expected SwiGLU correction is negative and much smaller.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.2 gives a positive one-step increment for similarity below exact collapse, increasing monotonically with the amount of attention. Theorem 3.4 gives a negative SwiGLU increment bounded near 0.011 under the stated initialization. In the 48-layer stack, measured branchwise increments follow the predicted sign and scale across 1x/2x/4x sublayer-variance sweeps, although the authors acknowledge visible curve mismatch.

key_findings.claim: Subtracting the uniform causal-prefix component suppresses most initialization-time similarity growth, supporting that component as a driver in the paper's surrogate sense.
key_findings.evidence: The intervention replaces attention P by P minus alpha C_n. Increasing alpha from zero to one uniformly reduces layerwise token-similarity growth, and alpha one removes most of it. Separately, averaging 32 random initializations shows the actual mean attention matrix differs from C_n by about 2.7% at layer 1, 1.2% at layer 48, and 2.1% on average in relative Frobenius norm.

key_findings.claim: In an exact- or near-collapse regime, growth of the pre-RMS residual norm can make backward transport contractive through many successive Post-Norm sublayers, whereas Pre-Norm preserves an identity gradient path.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.6 bounds each step by c(y, alpha) = alpha times square-root(d) divided by residual norm; if c is uniformly below one, early gradients decay geometrically. Proposition D.1 extends the condition to sufficiently near-collapse states, and Proposition D.2 proves that an output-projection gradient step strictly increases pre-normalization norm at exact collapse when the update is nonzero. In Pre-Norm, the RMS Jacobian affects only the sublayer path rather than the skip gradient.

key_findings.claim: Collapsing 48-layer Post-Norm runs exhibit the predicted temporal conjunction of residual-norm growth, RMS contraction, and orders-of-magnitude loss of early-layer gradients, but the diagnostics do not identify what initiates the transition.
key_findings.evidence: At peak learning rate 8e-4, last-layer similarity and loss transition around step 2644. Sublayer gradient contribution factors mostly remain below 2.5, while the RMS factors fall enough that most combined c values cross below one; early-layer gradients then drop by orders of magnitude while late-layer gradients remain comparatively stable. The pattern repeats around step 1979 for another seed and at 1.2e-3, 1.5e-3, and 1.8e-3; a 6e-4 control trains for 40,000 steps without collapse and has stable diagnostics.

key_findings.claim: At exact token collapse, the best shared prediction is the empirical label-frequency distribution, and once that prediction is attained all parameter gradients in collapsed and downstream layers vanish.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.8 lower-bounds near-collapse cross-entropy by frequency entropy minus a term proportional to distance from rank one and the LM-head norm. Its exact-collapse proof minimizes shared-row cross-entropy over one distribution, and the backward proof propagates zero column-sum gradients through multi-head attention, SwiGLU, and RMSNorm. Warmup and no-warmup collapsed runs stay near frequency-loss references constructed at matching label scopes.

method.core_idea: Use token similarity as a one-dimensional state variable to join an initialization-time forward model of causal prefix averaging with a training-time backward model of RMSNorm contraction, then characterize the exact rank-one endpoint through its optimal shared output distribution and gradients.
method.mechanism: The forward theory replaces random causal attention by uniform prefix averaging, closes the token Gram matrix with one equal-correlation parameter, and approximates an expected ratio by a ratio of expectations to derive attention and SwiGLU similarity increments. The backward theory factors gradient transport into an observed sublayer contribution alpha and the RMSNorm Jacobian, proves exact/near-collapse contraction conditions, and shows output-projection steps grow the pre-RMS norm at exact collapse. A separate theorem derives the frequency-loss floor and zero gradients. Experiments use matched 48-layer, approximately 180M-parameter Llama-2-style Pre/Post-Norm stacks on C4, initialization variance sweeps, a prefix-component subtraction intervention, transition-window gradient instrumentation, multiple learning rates/seeds, and pooled frequency-loss references.
assumptions: At random initialization, mean causal attention is close enough to uniform prefix averaging that C_n captures the dominant similarity effect.
The token Gram matrix can be represented by one equal off-diagonal correlation fixed by token similarity.
A ratio of expected projected and total energies accurately approximates expected token similarity at the studied width.
Single-head Gaussian theory with folded value/output projection transfers qualitatively to multi-head SwiGLU decoders with learned RMS gain and epsilon.
The measured sublayer contribution alpha remains bounded enough that residual-norm-dependent RMS shrinkage determines the sign of backward transport.
Exact-collapse proofs describe a sufficiently broad near-collapse neighborhood, despite the strict equality assumptions in several results.
Frequency distributions estimated over the selected sequence, batch, or pooled stream are the appropriate collapsed-output reference for each experiment.

techniques.role: Measures the fraction of hidden-state energy shared across token rows, equaling one exactly at row-constant rank collapse.
Approximates random causal softmax attention by uniform averaging over each available prefix to derive closed-form similarity growth.
Compresses the token Gram matrix to a single similarity-dependent off-diagonal correlation.
Separately predicts and measures positive attention amplification and negative SwiGLU damping.
Subtracts increasing multiples of the causal prefix-average matrix from attention to test whether similarity amplification disappears.
Multiplies the empirical sublayer gradient contribution by the analytical RMSNorm shrinkage factor to identify contractive layers.
Tracks residual norm, contraction factors, similarity, loss, and per-layer parameter gradients immediately around collapse.
Computes the entropy of empirical next-token frequencies as the best possible loss for a shared prediction at all positions.

evaluations.setting: 48-layer 180M-parameter training-matched Post-Norm and Pre-Norm stacks at initialization with 1x/2x/4x sublayer variance
evaluations.metric: One-step change in token similarity by attention and SwiGLU branch
evaluations.result: Attention increments are positive and follow the theorem's scale; SwiGLU increments are negative and much smaller. Post-Norm saturates toward high similarity earlier than Pre-Norm.
evaluations.baseline: Closed-form Theorems 3.2 and 3.4 under the same current similarity

evaluations.setting: Initialization-time attention replacement P minus alpha C_n
evaluations.metric: Layerwise token-similarity growth as alpha increases from 0 to 1
evaluations.result: Growth decreases monotonically and is mostly removed at alpha=1; mean P differs from C_n by about 1.2-2.7% across layers over 32 initializations.

evaluations.setting: C4 Post-Norm training at peak learning rate 8e-4, transition near optimizer step 2644
evaluations.metric: Similarity, loss, sublayer alpha, RMS shrinkage, combined c, and per-layer gradient norms
evaluations.result: Alpha mostly stays below 2.5; RMS factors and most c values fall sharply and cross below one; early-layer gradients drop by orders of magnitude while later gradients remain relatively stable.
evaluations.baseline: Pre-transition window in the same run

evaluations.setting: Repeated collapse diagnostics at another seed and peak learning rates 1.2e-3, 1.5e-3, and 1.8e-3
evaluations.result: The qualitative contraction and early-gradient-loss pattern repeats, with the second 8e-4 run transitioning near step 1979.
evaluations.baseline: A 6e-4 Post-Norm run that remains noncollapsed for 40,000 steps and keeps stable diagnostics

evaluations.setting: No-warmup full-training, one-batch, and one-sequence collapse plus warmup runs at 1.2e-3, 1.5e-3, and 1.8e-3
evaluations.metric: Post-collapse cross-entropy versus empirical frequency entropy
evaluations.result: Each collapsed loss stays near the frequency-loss curve computed from the chosen matching label collection.
evaluations.baseline: Theorem 3.8 frequency optimum, using 500M, 0.5M, or 2,048 labels according to scope

limitations: Author-stated: the analysis does not explain what triggers the abrupt rise in last-layer similarity and loss at a particular optimizer step.
Author-stated: initialization formulas rely on equal-correlation, uniform-prefix, and ratio-of-expectations approximations; the empirical attention curve retains visible mismatch.

Reviewer-identified: P minus alpha C_n is no longer a row-stochastic nonnegative attention matrix for alpha greater than zero, so the intervention removes prefix averaging while introducing signed, reduced-row-sum mixing; it does not uniquely isolate a valid attention component.

Reviewer-identified: the exact theory removes learned RMS gain and epsilon, folds value/output matrices, and begins with one head, whereas experiments use the standard multi-head learned-gain implementation and AdamW.

Reviewer-identified: alpha is defined from the observed ratio of sublayer input/output gradient norms; the contraction theorem becomes conditional on a measured quantity rather than independently predicting when sublayers compensate RMS shrinkage.

Reviewer-identified: transition-window measurements establish temporal association, but residual-norm growth and weak gradients may both be consequences of collapse; no intervention that restores the RMS factor demonstrates repair causally.
Reviewer-identified: strict residual-norm growth is proved only for one output-matrix gradient step at exact collapse, not for the complete AdamW update in a near-collapsed network.
Reviewer-identified: all training evidence uses one 48-layer, roughly 180M architecture/corpus; scale, depth, optimizer, data, and architecture generality are unknown.
Reviewer-identified: the manuscript does not report full seed counts, uncertainty intervals, or matched collapse rates across learning rates and normalization placements.

Reviewer-identified: the pooled 500M-token frequency reference is selected because it matches better than per-sequence averaging, while the exact theorem is stated for one sequence; output-distribution agreement itself is not measured.
failure_modes: Causal prefix averaging repeatedly increases shared token energy faster than the feed-forward branch can restore diversity.
Post-Norm renormalizes the whole residual path, so pre-normalization norm growth shrinks both skip and sublayer gradients at every depth step.
Many mildly contractive blocks compound into orders-of-magnitude gradient loss before the signal reaches the layers that created high similarity.
Once every token row is identical, the model can only emit one shared distribution and converges toward marginal token frequencies rather than contextual predictions.
At the shared frequency output, collapsed attention and feed-forward parameter gradients vanish, leaving a high-loss near-stationary state.
A learning rate that is safe before residual norms grow crosses into an unrecoverable regime after a sudden state change.
A diagnostic based only on final loss notices collapse after early-layer repair gradients have already disappeared.
The prefix-subtraction remedy yields signed attention and may improve similarity while breaking probabilistic mixing or downstream computation.
reusable_insights: Separate entry into a bad representation regime from the backward mechanism that makes the regime sticky; they may require different interventions.
Track a low-dimensional state variable jointly with the exact gradient-transport factors that could move it, rather than examining activation or gradients alone.
For Post-Norm systems, log pre-normalization residual norms and pre/post-normalization gradient ratios during training, especially around loss spikes.
A row-stochastic causal operator's prefix-average component is a useful null model for token homogenization at initialization.
Pre-Norm's stability advantage can be understood structurally: normalization does not multiply the identity skip gradient.
Characterize a collapsed model's best achievable predictor and parameter gradients, not only the decline of representation rank.
Use stable learning-rate controls and repeated transition windows to distinguish collapse-specific diagnostics from ordinary depth effects.
open_questions: What optimizer-state, batch, or activation event triggers the abrupt transition from high-but-stable similarity to collapse?
Can a causal intervention on pre-RMS norm or RMS backward scale restore early-layer gradients and reverse an incipient collapse?
Can the sublayer contribution alpha be bounded prospectively from weights, attention entropy, or Jacobian spectra instead of measured after backpropagation?
Is there a valid row-stochastic replacement that removes only the harmful prefix eigenmode while retaining causal attention semantics?
How do collapse thresholds scale with depth, width, context length, learning rate, warmup, and optimizer parameterization?
Do the same frequency-loss and zero-gradient endpoint arise in billion-parameter Post-Norm models with modern stabilization methods?
Does empirical output probability actually approach the predicted pooled frequency vector, or does loss agreement hide a different shared distribution?
How does this scalar token-similarity account relate quantitatively to depth and width spectral gaps in multi-head attention?

competitive_landscape.title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
competitive_landscape.difference: Xiong et al. use mean-field theory to show large output-layer Post-LN gradients at initialization and explain why warmup helps, while Pre-LN gradients are better behaved. The present paper instead follows causal decoders into a training-time high-similarity state and attributes irreversibility to residual-norm-dependent RMS contraction plus a collapsed frequency endpoint.

competitive_landscape.title: Signal Propagation in Transformers: Theoretical Perspectives and the Role of Rank Collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: Noci et al. show at initialization that rank collapse causes query/key gradients to vanish and propose depth-dependent residual scaling. This paper separates attention-driven entry from RMSNorm-mediated repair failure during actual Post-Norm training, includes SwiGLU, and derives the shared frequency predictor at exact collapse.

competitive_landscape.title: Why 'classic' Transformers are shallow and how to make them go deep
competitive_landscape.difference: Yu and Zhang already use token similarity to prove linear escalation from attention's invariant leading eigenspace and spectral gap and propose subtracting excessive similarity in Post-Norm encoders. The current work adapts the scalar analysis to causal prefix attention, adds a SwiGLU correction, and contributes the training-time RMS repair and frequency-loss results.

competitive_landscape.title: Mind the Gap: a Spectral Analysis of Rank Collapse and Signal Propagation in Attention Layers
competitive_landscape.difference: Naderi et al. use random-matrix theory to distinguish rank collapse in depth and in width, identify the softmax attention spectral gap, and remove outlier eigenvalues. This paper uses a coarser equal-correlation/prefix-average surrogate but connects it to optimizer-time residual norms, gradient transport, and the collapsed loss floor.

competitive_landscape.title: Exact Attention Sensitivity and the Geometry of Transformer Stability
competitive_landscape.difference: Emadi derives exact softmax-Jacobian sensitivity and sequence-length-independent Lipschitz bounds, proving Post-LN compounds normalization Jacobians and validating on 774M models. This paper's novel conditional factor is the growth of pre-RMS norm after similarity collapse and its link to failed repair, but it has smaller-scale and less exact empirical evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: Post-LayerNorm Is Back: Stable, ExpressivE, and Deep
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen and Wei identify the ResNet-style Post-LN residual pathway as the main gradient failure and replace it with a Highway connection, reporting stable training beyond 1,000 layers. This paper offers a two-stage similarity/RMS mechanism and endpoint characterization but proposes no validated stabilizer or extreme-depth result.

competitive_landscape.title: From Condensation to Rank Collapse: A Two-Stage Analysis of Transformer Training Dynamics
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen and Luo already use a two-stage label for small-initialization training: parameter condensation followed by key-query-driven rank collapse in a simplified single-layer setting. The current two stages are materially different—causal attention amplification at initialization and RMS-mediated backward repair failure in a 48-layer Post-Norm decoder—but the generic two-stage framing is not itself novel.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: this is a new two-stage account in which causal prefix averaging first amplifies token similarity and growing pre-RMS residual norms then contract the backward signal needed to repair it; a collapsed network is further characterized by a frequency-distribution optimum and vanishing parameter gradients. Primary work already explains Post-LN warmup, initialization-time rank collapse and query/key gradient loss, token-similarity escalation, attention spectral gaps, and repeated normalization-Jacobian contraction; another paper already uses a two-stage rank-collapse framing. Reviewer inference: the substantive incremental novelty is the integration of causal-prefix/SwiGLU forward formulas with transition-window RMS diagnostics and the exact collapsed-frequency endpoint. The manuscript does not yet causally explain transition onset or prove that residual-norm growth is the training-time cause rather than a companion symptom, so its mechanism should be presented as a well-supported conditional account rather than a complete cause of Post-Norm collapse.
reviewer_notes: All 48 pages were inspected, including forward approximations, concentration and RMS corrections, exact/near-collapse backward proofs, multi-head/SwiGLU zero-gradient proof, repeated learning-rate/seed diagnostics, and the noncollapsed control. Page anchors distinguish theorem statements from appendix proofs and empirical checks. The prefix subtraction's loss of stochasticity, the conditional nature of alpha, and the pooled-frequency choice are reviewer inferences. Competitive identifiers and mechanisms were verified on primary arXiv/JMLR records.
